name: Palmitoyl hexapeptide-12

card.summary: An elastin-fragment cosmetic peptide (Biopeptide EL) with lab-level evidence and no clinical trials found.

quick.overview:
Palmitoyl hexapeptide-12 is a lab-made peptide based on an elastin sequence, added to anti-ageing creams for elasticity.

Only early laboratory research exists; no clinical trial was found.
quick.mechanism: It is described as a self-assembling peptide that interacts with skin components and may alter skin mechanics, based on a 2025 imaging study.
quick.risks: No ingredient-specific harms were found; safety frameworks for cosmetic peptides are still evolving.

lead: Palmitoyl hexapeptide-12, sold as Biopeptide EL, is a synthetic fatty-acid-linked peptide derived from a repeating elastin sequence and used in anti-aging creams. People apply products containing it aiming for firmer, more elastic-looking skin and a smoother appearance of fine lines.

It belongs to the family of cosmetic signal peptides, which includes palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 (Matrixyl), a five-amino-acid peptide attached to a 16-carbon fatty chain that the manufacturer Sederma launched in 2000. [3] The fatty chain is described as helping such molecules enter skin lipids. [3] The idea behind the group is that short protein fragments could prompt skin to behave as it does in younger tissue, a goal that matters to people because loss of elastic fibres is one feature of ageing skin. [3][5]

A 2025 laboratory study using label-free imaging techniques tracked the peptide in full-thickness human skin, found it permeated the stratum corneum and epidermis while forming a gel, and reported that it strengthened and repaired the skin barrier after lipid removal in tests.[1] No clinical trial results were found.

chain: Peptide applied in a cream or serum
Penetrates upper skin layers and interacts with skin components
angle.text: People use creams with this peptide hoping for firmer-looking skin and softened fine lines. The 2025 ex vivo study supports penetration and barrier-strengthening in skin samples.

infobox: 2025 ex vivo imaging study in human skin [1]

paras: The peptide is promoted in anti-aging products for firmness and elasticity. Researchers describe cosmetic self-assembling peptides of this kind as interacting with skin structures, though their short-term impact on composition and mechanics had been unclear before the 2025 study. [1]

The wider category of palmitoyl matrikine peptides is described as messenger peptides said to activate genes involved in extracellular matrix renewal, an explanation Wikipedia flags as needing citation for Matrixyl. [3]

Wikipedia's elastin article reports that elastin has a half-life of over 78 years in humans, but that its function can change with age: a 2014 in vivo multiphoton study reported age-related reductions in measured dermal elastin and collagen, and more recent 3D imaging found fewer, more fragmented elastic fibres in older skin. A 2022 comparison of people aged 18 to 25 and 70 to 75 found altered elastin density and fibre organisation, especially in chronically sun-exposed areas. [5] Elastin-derived peptides such as this one are marketed on the premise that they can address the visible result, which is a loss of firmness and elasticity.

In the 2025 study, orbital trapping secondary ion mass spectrometry distinguished the peptide's sol and gel forms and tracked its self-assembly and penetration, and stimulated Raman scattering and mechanical testing showed barrier strengthening after delipidation, with co-assembly with native skin molecules shown in vitro and in ex vivo histology. [1] The study used full-thickness human skin samples and reported that the peptide permeated the stratum corneum and epidermis and started to form a gel by using the skin's own ions. [1] The authors describe the work as a methodological benchmark for measuring cosmetic peptide effects on skin mechanics. [1]

Matrixyl (palmitoyl pentapeptide-4, Pal-KTTKS) was launched by Sederma in 2000 and is described as a matrikine that boosts extracellular matrix synthesis, with in vitro and in vivo studies by the manufacturer and independent groups including a 2005 study on photoaged facial skin; Wikipedia tags its anti-wrinkle claim as needing a medical citation. [3] GHK-Cu and caffeoyl hexapeptide-9 are other cosmetic peptides named in the same literature. [2][3]
A T Nation member asking about peptides to improve healing times, scarring and results listed TB-500, GHK, Biopeptide EL and Matrixyl together as options. [4] No replies are recorded in the thread.

No studies found in human clinical trials of palmitoyl hexapeptide-12 itself. A 2025 ex vivo study monitored the peptide in human skin layers with non-invasive techniques and assessed its mechanical interaction with skin components. [1]

A 2026 paper proposes a bioinformatic framework for safety evaluation of cosmetic peptides as the industry shifts away from animal testing; it tested palmitoyl hexapeptide-12 along with caffeoyl hexapeptide-9, palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 and other peptides using six bioinformatic tools, and the framework correctly flagged toxin peptides such as amanitin and conotoxin in the same test set. [2] No ingredient-specific adverse-effect data were found.

timeline.event: Sederma launches Matrixyl (palmitoyl pentapeptide-4), the best-known cosmetic signal peptide. [3]
Imaging study tracks palmitoyl hexapeptide-12 in full-thickness human skin. [1]
Bioinformatic safety framework for cosmetic peptides published, including this peptide. [2]
